title: fix(cli)!: objectstack build writes the runtime module whenever a callable still needs it (#22853)
body:
Fixes #22853
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong (measured on `origin/main` `69d4218058`)

`objectstack build` decided whether to write `objectstack-runtime.*.mjs` from `lowering.count - lowering.bodyExtracted` plus the extraction warnings (`compile.ts`, the `needsBundle` line). `count` is per callable, `bodyExtracted` per lowered slot, so a callable lowered at two slots cancelled a `functions` entry beside it. A tsx probe over `lowerCallables` at the base:

| shape | count | bodyExtracted | old `needsBundle` | `bodylessCallables` (PR #22849) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| card: hook + `functions` entry, top level AND `packages[0].manifest` | 2 | 2 | false | `function 'pb_score'` |
| addendum: one handler shared by two hooks + a `functions` entry | 2 | 2 | false | `function 'pb_score'` |
| one function as a lowered hook handler AND a `functions` entry | 1 | 1 | false | **empty** |
| one function as a hook handler (hook face refuses it) AND an action target (action face lowers it) | 1 | 1 | true (warning) | **empty** |
| CONTROL: all body-only, one walk / two walks | 2 / 1 | 2 / 2 | false | empty |

At the door (`bin/run-dev.js build`, the ablation leg below), the first three printed `Skipping legacy runtime bundle (all 2 callables are body-only)` (twice) and `(all 1 callables are body-only)`, exited 0 and wrote no module.

**PM mechanism assumption 2 holds.** `compile.ts` alone covers the card's shape and the addendum's, but not the third row: `bodylessCallables` dropped every ref some slot lowered (`[...unlowered].filter(([ref]) => !loweredRefs.has(ref))`), so a function lowered for its hook read as body-only although its `functions` entry has no body slot. The fourth row is the same hole in the other direction: a refused hook was dropped because the action lowered the same function, so `--strict-body` passed a hook that ships with no body.

## The fix

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts` (the producer of the population).** Each slot that leaves a callable unlowered now says which kind it is: `refused`, `functions-entry` or `authored-body`. A `refused` or `functions-entry` slot has no body at all, so another slot lowering the same function does not take the callable off `bodylessCallables`. Only an `authored-body` slot is taken off by a lowering elsewhere (every slot then has a body), which keeps PR #22849's verdict for that case. A callable bound at several slots reports its strongest row (refusal, then `functions` entry, then authored body), so the row is the extractor's refusal whenever one exists. New export `isExtractionRefusal(row)`, a type guard over the same rows.
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts`.** `needsBundle = lowering.bodylessCallables.length > 0`. `stillNeeded` and the `|| bodyExtractionWarnings.length > 0` term are gone: every refusal is a row of the list, so the term could add nothing. The default-path warning, its summary line and the `--no-runtime-bundle` message count `refusedCallables` (the list's refusal rows), each refused handler once.
- **Landing point.** The claim's surface named `lower-callables.ts` only if a single-walk member needed the population to change. Measured: one does (row 3), so it lands there. `extract-hook-body.ts`, `detect-free-identifiers.ts` and `hook-body.ts` are untouched. No `packages/spec` change.

**The decision only moves from skip to write.** If `count - bodyExtracted > 0`, some callable has no lowered slot, and every registered callable is either lowered somewhere or noted unlowered, so it is a row. Every refusal is a row too. A unit pin asserts the implication over eight shapes.

## What moves for consumers (changeset `minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in its body)

- `objectstack build` writes the module for the shapes above. Nothing it wrote before is skipped.
- `--no-runtime-bundle` now refuses those stacks (exit 1); it passed them while the entry had no implementation.
- `--strict-body` now refuses a function bound at a lowered slot AND as a `functions` entry or at a refused slot. PR #22849 pinned the third row as passing (`a callable lowered at ANY slot is not a row`); triage's grade on this card rules it the other way, so that pin is replaced.
- The default-path warning counts a refused handler once, not once per slot. `--json` `bodyExtractionWarnings` is unchanged (still one record per slot).

## Tests (all at `b464a20646`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: 281 files / 4245 tests passed, 2 failed at `5cbd9c5ceb`. Both were source-text pins on `compile.ts`: `truncation-remainder-notices` (the precedent loop's list is now `refusedCallables`) and `validate-build-gate-parity` (`isExtractionRefusal` classified under local helpers). After that update, the 4 affected unit files passed: 112 tests.
- New unit pins in `test/lower-callables.test.ts`: the `functions` entry beside a lowered hook is a row; a refused slot beside a lowered action is a row; an authored-body slot IS taken off by a lowering elsewhere; strongest-row precedence; a two-walk all-clean CONTROL; old-decision-implies-new over eight shapes.
- New integration pin `test/build-runtime-bundle-bodyless.test.ts` (spawns `os build`; queue tier, not nightly): `--project integration` 6/6 passed. The two-level stack and the shared-handler stack write the module, the artifact points at it, and `pb_score` runs through `@objectstack/runtime`'s `loadArtifactBundle` (answers 1). The hook-and-`functions` stack writes the module, and its `functions` entry resolves to a callable. CONTROLS: an all-body-only stack (one walk and two walks) still prints the skip line and leaves no module in `dist/`. A refused hook walked twice reads `1 handler could not be lowered` and one bullet.
- Also run: `build-strict-body-count.test.ts` (integration, green); nightly `hook-body-build-reach.e2e`, `build-json-failure-warnings.e2e`, `build-multi-package-artifact.e2e` under `OS_TEST_TIERS=nightly`: 25/25.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes both new or edited test files, with no errors in them.

**Ablations** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor hit 1 to 0, blob changed, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty, plus a trap leg that re-proves both files. All are source edits run through tsx, so there is no `dist/` leg):
- A, the population filter reverted to `!loweredRefs.has(ref)`: 3 red (the two new unit pins and the door's hook-and-`functions` pin), 28 green.
- B, `needsBundle` reverted to the old arithmetic: 3 red at the door (two-level, shared-handler, hook-and-`functions`), each printing the skip line; CONTROLS and the warning pin green.
- C, the warning count reverted to `bodyExtractionWarnings.length`: the double-walked refusal reads `2 handlers could not be lowered`, red.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on the final tree derives the same 65 commands as the dispatch. All 65 exit 0 at `b464a20646`. Reconciled: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 65 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).` Three gates first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: unbuilt packages, then a contended build OOM-killed at 137). After a targeted rebuild they read: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` 107 entry points load; `check:i18n-coverage` `OK (13 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`; `check:type-check-debt` `surplus: none`. Also run: the four roster gates whose roster sits under a touched directory (`check-changeset-fixed`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`), all exit 0.

**Lint, proven narrowing.** The 6 touched code files (2 source, 4 test), `eslint --no-inline-config --format json`: 6 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Population: `--print-config` resolves a config (5 to 6 rules) for every file. Invariance: `parserOptions.project` and `projectService` are null for each file (this repo never enables type-aware linting), so this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- **Found beside this card, not fixed here (class (a), measured at the door on this branch):** `lowerCallables` re-keys a `functions` map entry by the ref it registered.
  - `functions: { pr_score: tidy }` beside hook `pr_tidy` bound to the same `tidy` ships `functions: { pr_tidy: 'pr_tidy' }`, so the authored name `pr_score` is gone.
  - A hook `pc_score` (refused) beside a distinct `functions: { pc_score: scoreFn }` ships `functions` keys `pc_score__2` (a bare string, no callable after `loadArtifactBundle`) and `pc_score`, which is `scoreFn`. The hook's handler ref `pc_score` therefore resolves to the `functions` entry's code.
  - The runtime module's entry collector keys hooks by name and functions by authored key, so the two collide. Reported for the seat to file.
- `--json` `bodyExtractionWarnings` and `handlersBundled` keep their per-slot / per-callable meaning. They are machine-read payload keys and were left alone.
- The PR body's `Clause-②: no` is the claim's line verbatim. The changeset declares `(narrowing)` because `--no-runtime-bundle` and `--strict-body` refuse stacks they passed. The report names this for the seat.
